quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You can pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street only if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street, you must be able to see the road ahead clearly, return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and have a vehicle that can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads. These areas freeze faster than sunny roads and take longer to dry.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian legally has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: What driving technique helps prevent crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highways as quickly as possible.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: When roads are snow-covered or icy, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. These are the most important ways to avoid crashes.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal has the same rules as:
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane ends or the road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. This sign warns you that a lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control signs, yield to the car coming from your right.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is risky.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a white dashed line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: In snowy weather, what should happen to your following distance?

options.text: It does not matter what your following distance is.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should increase.
questions.explanation: In snow, slow down and leave more space between your car and the car ahead. Icy roads require more time to stop than dry roads.

questions.question: Round signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other cars. Drive with the flow of traffic, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: The driver should honk their horn.
The driver should pass the animal as closely as possible.
The driver should be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't scare it.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign indicates:

options.text: That the speed limit is 20 mph.
The beginning of a reduced speed zone.
The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.
The end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit when you see the beginning sign. The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to get ahead of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of room. They don't have the protection that cars provide. Passing too fast or too close can force them off course.

questions.question: When should drivers use one-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving activity.
When avoiding a hazard at a high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing, using signals, turning on the radio, or activating windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When backing, using signals, turning on the radio, or activating windshield wipers.
questions.explanation: Use one hand on the wheel only when backing or using vehicle controls like wipers, lights, or signals that require you to reach away from the steering wheel.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less. Take these steps to make nighttime driving safer for you and others on the road.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they cross against the light or are not being careful.

questions.question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you from driving and increase your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should wait for a minimum ____ gap in traffic.
questions.correctAnswerText: Four- or five-second
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, find a four- or five-second gap in the lane you want to enter. Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder. Adjust your speed and steer into the lane. Then cancel your signal.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to pass before you go.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: Signs that are orange are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. They are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Which is a characteristic of a defensive driver?
questions.correctAnswerText: Alertness
questions.explanation: A defensive driver stays alert and watches for danger. They predict possible problems and are ready to act.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Decreases the number of driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you overconfident, and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug can be a crime.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas and let your vehicle slow before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas to slow your vehicle first, then apply the brake smoothly. This lights your brake lights and gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A bicyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass them?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass the bicyclist while giving them plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. It is the bicyclist's job to get out of your way.
Do not pass the bicyclist until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk at the bicyclist to warn them you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass the bicyclist while giving them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Do not go too fast or get too close. You could kick up rocks or push them with air from your car. Leave at least 3 feet between your mirror and the bicyclist. On faster roads or with groups of bicyclists, leave at least 5 feet. Do not honk unless needed. Unexpected honking can startle riders and cause them to crash.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green, but there is heavy oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go ahead because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for that traffic to pass before you turn. You can enter the intersection if the light is green and no other car ahead of you is turning left.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing ahead. Watch for people crossing the street. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The first driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
The last driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first driver to arrive has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The car that gets there first goes first. If two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check for traffic you cannot see in your mirror.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Make sure no other car is in the lane you want to enter. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on cloudy days. Use low beam when another car is within 1,000 feet ahead or within 500 feet behind you. Always use low beam in bad weather.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: When you have more than one hazard, deal with one at a time. Do not try to squeeze between an oncoming car and a bicyclist at the same time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers about dangerous road conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible hazards. Always obey warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers need to see your car clearly.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey all signs and signals. Trains, cars, and bicyclists all share the road.
